# igni as a whole

Where these methods are:

- `igni` — on `IgniClient` itself

Every method here is generated from igni-core's RPC contract; its documentation is igni's own. The examples run inside an `async` function with `igni` an open `IgniClient` and `session` one of its sessions ([Quick start](/docs/sdk/igni-client/quick-start)).

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`igni.check_for_update()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/igni#igni-check-for-update) | Ask whether a newer igni release is available. |
| [`igni.group_policy()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/igni#igni-group-policy) | Read which organisation group's policy igni follows. |

## igni.check_for_update()

Ask whether a newer igni release is available.

```python
async def check_for_update(self) -> UpdateAvailable | None
```

Takes no arguments. Returns the newer release — its version, the
version installed, where to get it — or `null` when there is none
(or update checks are switched off). Fails when the check could not
reach an answer (network, HTTP status, an unreadable reply), so a
caller can tell that from "no update".

Takes no arguments.

**Returns** [`UpdateAvailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/models-reference#updateavailable)` | None`.

**How long** `network` — Asks a server — igni server, an MCP server, PyPI — and waits for its answer.
The client waits up to 60 seconds.

**Access** [`client`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — any connection igni admitted.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `check_for_update`, scope `igni`, area `models`; igni answers with `rpc_response`.

**Example**

```python
check_for_update = await igni.check_for_update()
if check_for_update is not None:
    print(check_for_update.available, check_for_update.current_version)
```

## igni.group_policy()

Read which organisation group's policy igni follows.

```python
async def group_policy(self) -> GroupPolicyPackResult
```

Takes no arguments. Returns the group's id and name, when its
policy pack was fetched, how many entries it has and the default
model it sets; nulls and zero when igni follows no group.

Takes no arguments.

**Returns** [`GroupPolicyPackResult`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/models-reference#grouppolicypackresult).

**How long** `io` — Reads or writes the project, the session's database or the disk; a few seconds at most.
The client waits up to 30 seconds.

**Access** [`client`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — any connection igni admitted.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `get_group_policy`, scope `igni`, area `panels`; igni answers with `rpc_response`.

**Example**

```python
group_policy = await igni.group_policy()
print(group_policy.default_model, group_policy.entry_count)
```
